items.detail: Fed Chair **Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole keynote on Friday at 10:00 ET**, closing a symposium that runs August 27-29 under the theme 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy' — his last set-piece before the September 16 FOMC.
items.why: The July minutes showed Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissenting for a hike, so any hint Warsh shares that bias would push the 30-year back toward last week's 5.33% high and extend the duration repricing that cost the index 1.4%, while a patient, data-dependent tone would relieve exactly the pressure that has been the dominant equity driver.

items.detail: **Wednesday is the data day**: July core PCE is expected at **+0.2% m/m, leaving the annual rate at 3.3%**, alongside the second estimate of Q2 GDP (consensus **1.5%**, down from 2.1%) and July durable goods — with a 5-year note auction the same afternoon and 2-year and 7-year sales bracketing it on Tuesday and Thursday.
items.why: A hot core PCE lands directly on a long end already refusing to absorb supply after two failed Treasury buyback escalations, so the auction tails would do the damage rather than the print itself; a soft number plus a soft GDP revision is the one combination that lets equities rally on growth weakness.

items.detail: **Nvidia reports Q2 FY2027 after the close on Wednesday**, with consensus near **$91.9bn in revenue and about $2.08 EPS** against company guidance of $91bn plus or minus 2%.
items.why: Semiconductors were the first casualty of last week's yield move and the Nasdaq's 2% loss, so a beat-and-raise is the clearest available offset to the rates story — but landing hours after core PCE means a hot inflation print could bury a good number, and an in-line guide would leave the index with nothing to lean on into Friday.

items.detail: Treasury Secretary Bessent is set to unveil the **Iran sanctions package on Monday** — the 'economic D-Day' escalation — with Brent starting the week near **$93** after a second straight 6% weekly gain and Iran's security council threatening Hormuz ship seizures in response.
items.why: India imports roughly 85% of its crude, so this is the single input that sets the import bill, the inflation path and the rupee's floor at 95.70 all at once; secondary sanctions on buyers would also close off the Iranian barrels Indian state refiners had been weighing, while any sign of a negotiated off-ramp is the fastest way to unwind the risk premium.

items.detail: **Tuesday is the August monthly F&O expiry** for Nifty and the index-derivative complex, with the index carrying in at **24,252** — below the 24,450-24,750 band where the 200-day, 50-week and 100-week moving averages converge, and above support at 24,000-23,800.
items.why: Two consecutive down weeks and a seven-session losing streak have left positioning short into a settlement, so expiry-week unwinding can force a squeeze toward 24,400 that has nothing to do with fundamentals — but the moving-average cluster overhead means only a close above 24,750 changes the range, and a break of 24,000 hands the tape back to the sellers.

items.detail: With the domestic earnings calendar largely emptied, **FII flows and the rupee are the week's swing factors**, and both key off Wednesday's US data and Friday's Warsh keynote — DIIs absorbed roughly ₹14,700 crore of buying last week against near-continuous FII selling, holding the drawdown to 0.5% and the rupee in a 30-paisa range near 95.7050.
items.why: Indian markets trade a session behind Wall Street, so a hawkish Warsh on Friday would hit Indian screens only on Monday while widening the rate differential that has been driving foreign outflows all month; the risk is that oil-driven importer hedging and FII selling arrive together, which is the one combination SIP-funded domestic buying has not had to absorb yet.

items.detail: **Warsh's Friday Jackson Hole debut** is the week's dominant catalyst for crypto too, because the symposium's stated theme is **'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy'** — putting stablecoins and payment rails on the agenda of a Fed Chair speaking days after Treasury's GENIUS Act rulemaking opened.
items.why: Bitcoin's 22% week was built on Treasury buybacks removing the rates cap on risk assets, so a speech that keeps further tightening at arm's length preserves the weaker-dollar, lower-yield backdrop the rally needs, while a hawkish surprise takes away the whole mechanism at once — and any direct remarks on stablecoin regulation would hit the payment tokens independently of the macro read.

items.detail: **Wednesday's core PCE** is the macro print that matters most, with bitcoin stalling near **$77,000** below the $79,400 high after spot ETFs took **$1.918bn across five sessions** last week — the strongest inflow stretch of the month heading into a month-end options settlement.
items.why: The rally was mechanically driven by more than $4bn of short liquidations rather than organic demand, which cuts both ways: a soft PCE that reinforces the easing path could pull the ETF bid through $80,000, but with the shorts already flushed there is no fuel left for a squeeze, so a hot print meets a market that is now long and has to sell rather than cover.

items.detail: Two supply events land early — **TON unlocks 1.33% of circulating supply (about $54.12m) on Monday** and Humanity's H token unlocks 7.92% (about $20m) on Tuesday — while miner-turned-AI-host **IREN reports FY2026 results after Thursday's close**.
items.why: Unlocks of this size only bite when the bid is thin, so they are a useful tell on whether last week's inflows were real allocation or squeeze-driven; IREN matters more as a read-through, since its split between bitcoin mining economics at $77,000 and an AI cloud business targeting over $4bn in revenue is the clearest public test of whether the equity market still values miners on hashprice or on datacentre capacity.

crossCuttingTheme: Every market is trading the same long-end-of-the-curve question this week, asked twice: Wednesday's core PCE and Q2 GDP revision arrive alongside 2-, 5- and 7-year auctions into a Treasury market that just rejected two buyback escalations, and Friday Warsh answers it in his Jackson Hole debut — with Bessent's Monday Iran sanctions keeping Brent near $93 as the inflation input that makes a dovish answer harder, which is the exact channel that repriced US megacaps, froze the rupee at 95.70 and handed crypto its $4bn short squeeze last week.
